headline: Broad Selloff Leaves Bulls on Defense as Tech Rout and Rising Yields Cloud the Open
body_html:
Wall Street enters Wednesday's pre-market in a cautious crouch after Tuesday's session delivered a decisive rebuke to growth and technology stocks. Declining issues outpaced advancers by more than three to one across our 549-name universe — 422 names lower against just 125 higher — with semiconductors off 2.36% and software sliding 2.42% to lead the damage. The 10-year Treasury yield pushed to its highest level since January 2025, a move traders are attributing partly to renewed Middle Eastern geopolitical tensions, and that rising-rate backdrop is doing technology bulls no favors this morning.

Energy was the lone sector to finish in the green Tuesday, gaining 0.89%, as agricultural-chemicals names CF Industries and Corteva advanced more than 3.8% apiece and fuel-cell outfit Bloom Energy added 3.55%. Healthcare eked out a fractional decline of 0.16%, a relative safe harbor in an otherwise bruising session. Consumer, homebuilders, and industrials all surrendered between 1.6% and 2.0%, suggesting the selling pressure was broad rather than narrowly concentrated.

At the open, attention will focus on Washington, where the House is pressing to avert a government shutdown amid resistance from hardline members, and on any fresh commentary around the artificial-intelligence trade, where token prices have hit record lows and at least one prominent desk has moved to lock in gains on a data-center position. The risk-off posture looks likely to persist until those overhangs begin to clear.

briefs.headline: Ten-Year Yield Reaches 16-Month High as Middle East Tensions Flare
briefs.body: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its loftiest level since January 2025 overnight, as revived Middle Eastern tensions pushed investors toward safe-haven positioning. The move is amplifying pressure on rate-sensitive growth stocks heading into Wednesday's open, keeping the technology sector on the back foot.

briefs.headline: AI Token Prices Collapse to Record Lows, Rattling Sentiment
briefs.body: Prices for artificial-intelligence tokens have fallen to all-time lows, adding another headwind to a sector already under pressure from rising yields. The development underscores mounting skepticism about near-term AI monetization, with at least one institutional desk trimming a data-center holding to protect accumulated gains.

briefs.headline: OpenAI Flags First Model to Clear a 'Critical' Cybersecurity Threshold
briefs.body: OpenAI disclosed that its Astra AI model has become the first it has developed to surpass what the company characterizes as a critical cybersecurity capability benchmark. The announcement adds a new dimension to the AI arms race and is drawing attention from enterprise security buyers and policymakers alike.

briefs.headline: House Races to Head Off Government Shutdown Ahead of Deadline
briefs.body: Congressional leaders are pushing to assemble enough votes to keep federal agencies funded, with a bloc of Republican hardliners complicating the path to a clean stopgap measure. Markets are monitoring the situation closely; a failure to reach agreement before the deadline could inject fresh volatility into an already unsettled tape.

briefs.headline: SharkNinja Leads Decliners with a 9% Plunge; Trucking and Cybersecurity Also Hit Hard
briefs.body: Consumer-products maker SharkNinja was Tuesday's steepest loser, shedding 9.13%, while connectivity chipmaker Credo Technology fell 8.65% and Cadence Design dropped 7.6%. CrowdStrike shed 6.9% and trucking carrier Saia lost 6.62%, illustrating how broadly the selling spread beyond any single theme.

briefs.headline: India's Economic Momentum Sharpens Investment Case as LNG Demand Surges
briefs.body: A stronger-than-expected Indian GDP reading is fueling talk of an impending investment boom in the subcontinent, even as the country's liquefied natural gas imports climbed to a six-year high despite elevated prices. The data points are lending support to the emerging-markets energy trade that helped lift the energy sector on Tuesday.
